headline: New orders grow, but profit and margins keep shrinking
summary_short: NVR earned $83.96 per diluted share on net income of $236.5 million in Q2 2026, down 23% and 29% y/y, as consolidated revenue fell 11% to $2.33 billion and homebuilding gross margin compressed to 19.2% from 21.5%.
summary_long: Homebuilding gross margin fell to 19.2% from 21.5% on higher lot costs, affordability-driven pricing pressure, weak consumer sentiment, and $21.7 million of contract land deposit impairments. Homebuilding revenue declined 11% to $2.28 billion as settlements fell 8% to 5,058 units even as new orders rose 9% to 5,885 units; average settlement price fell 3% to $450,700. Mortgage banking pretax income fell 14% to $25.4 million on 13% lower loan production. Net income of $236.5 million (-29% y/y) and diluted EPS of $83.96 (-23% y/y) reflect the margin and volume pressure. NVR repurchased $357.8 million of stock in the quarter; cash and equivalents fell to $1.20 billion and shareholders' equity to $3.39 billion. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Settlements and margins fell as affordability challenges and weak consumer sentiment pressured pricing, while orders still grew and land-deposit impairments added $21.7M of costs.
Margin compression was driven by higher lot costs, pricing pressure from affordability challenges and weak consumer sentiment, and about $21.7 million of contract land deposit impairments.
Homebuilding revenue fell as settlements dropped 8% to 5,058 units and average settlement price fell 3% to $450,700, even though new orders rose 9%.
Homebuilding segment income fell 30% y/y on margin compression and lower settlement volume; mortgage banking income also fell 14% y/y on lower loan production.
EPS fell less than net income's 29% drop because the diluted share count also fell year-over-year from continued buybacks, partially offsetting the earnings decline.

Tracks the homebuilding margin compression to 19.2% and 8% lower settlement volume; Yahoo's consolidated gross-profit concept nets somewhat differently than the release's own segment income statement.
Tracks the release's $318.6 million consolidated pretax income (-29% y/y ex rounding), driven by lower homebuilding segment income and lower mortgage banking income.
Since year-end 2025, retained earnings grew $434.8 million on net income, but treasury-stock purchases from buybacks grew faster, cutting total equity by $473.7 million.
NVR repurchased 54,716 shares for $357.8 million this quarter alone, continuing the multi-year share-count reduction from its buyback program.
